body.en: A *notice* informs a group about an event, a change or an instruction. Format: the name of the institution, the word NOTICE, the date, a heading (the subject in capitals or bold), the body, and the name and designation of the writer. The body answers what, when (date and time), where, who may take part, and whom to contact. A notice is brief, factual and usually in the third person or passive voice; it may be boxed.

A greeting such as Dear Ms Rao,

explanation.en: A notice is displayed for a group and headed NOTICE; an email has a subject line and a greeting to a reader. Both carry the date and the writer's name.

say.en: Sort each feature.

body.en: A *formal email* has the recipient's address, a short, specific subject line, a greeting (Dear Sir / Dear Ms Rao), a body that states the purpose in the first sentence and the details in short paragraphs, a polite closing line, and a sign-off (Regards / Yours sincerely) with the writer's name and details. It is concise and polite, avoids abbreviations and emojis, and mentions any attachment.

narration.en: A formal email has the recipient's address, a short, specific subject line, a greeting (Dear Sir / Dear Ms Rao), a body that states the purpose in the first sentence and the details in short paragraphs, a polite closing line, and a sign-off (Regards / Yours sincerely) with the writer's name and details. It is concise and polite, avoids abbreviations and emojis, and mentions any attachment.

say.en: A formal email has the recipient's address, a short, specific subject line, a greeting (Dear Sir divided by Dear Ms Rao), a body that states the purpose in the first sentence and the details in short paragraphs, a polite closing line, and a sign-off (Regards divided by Yours sincerely) with the writer's name and details. It is concise and polite, avoids abbreviations and emojis, and mentions any attachment. To, subject, greeting.
Purpose in the first sentence.
Short paragraphs; mention attachments.
Polite sign-off with name.

We will work under the supervision of Ms Nair. A list of the team members is __3__. I look forward to your reply. __4__, Kabir Khan, Class XI-B

options.en: Request for use of the laboratory

explanation.en: The subject states the purpose; "request" is polite; "attached" refers to an attachment; "Regards" is a suitable formal sign-off.

problem.en: Write a notice for your school informing students about a free eye check-up camp.

steps.en: MODERN PUBLIC SCHOOL, JAIPUR / NOTICE / 3 March
A free eye check-up camp will be held in the medical room on 10 March from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., in association with City Eye Hospital.
All students of Classes VI to XII may attend in their free periods. Students who wear spectacles should bring them.
Contact the undersigned for details. Anjali Verma, Head Girl.

answer.en: A complete notice: institution, NOTICE, date, heading, the facts, and the writer's name and designation.
